entities.name: Tourette syndrome
observations: A 2023 systematic review/meta-analysis of 12 studies (n=3,812) estimated pooled anxiety prevalence at 53.5% (95% CI 39.9–66.6%); prevalence increased with increasing mean age. The estimate was heterogeneous and included clinically diverse samples.

In a 2015 structured-interview cohort of 1,374 people with Tourette syndrome versus 1,142 unaffected family members, anxiety risk was increased (OR 1.4, 95% CI 1.0–1.9, p=.04) after accounting for OCD and ADHD.

In the same cohort, 72.1% met criteria for OCD or ADHD; excluding these conditions reduced the mean number of comorbid diagnoses from 2.1 to 0.9, so anxiety estimates require careful separation from OCD and ADHD.

entities.name: Persistent tic disorder
observations: Evidence beyond Tourette syndrome is limited. A 2021 analysis found psychiatric comorbidities other than OCD, ADHD, and substance-use disorders generally occurred at similar frequencies in persistent motor/vocal tic disorder and Tourette syndrome; this did not establish a precise anxiety prevalence versus tic-free controls.

entities.name: Anxiety excess in Tourette syndrome
observations: Clinical and comparative evidence supports higher prevalence of clinically significant anxiety in Tourette syndrome than in people without tic disorders, but exact estimates vary by age, setting, and measurement method.
